clauses.reason: Executive Order 6684-C of April 19, 1934 states: "do order that the said Electrical Contracting Chapter be and it is hereby approved, and that the previous approval of said Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry is hereby modified to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as modified by the addition thereto of said Electrical Contracting Chapter" That command is a approval of the Electrical Contracting Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry, and modification of the earlier approval of that code to cover the code as supplemented under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and it has legal effect only through that approval: under section 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, and under sections 3(c) and 3(f) violations were restrainable in equity and punishable as misdemeanors. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no other effective date, so the command ended as a prospective operative command on June 14, 1935. No earlier end is shown (see earlier_end_check). The June 16, 1935 expiry is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6684-C (April 19, 1934) is a approval of the Electrical Contracting Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry, and modification of the earlier approval of that code to cover the code as supplemented under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (page record checked; identity, date and subject confirmed against the census register and the WPA 1944 list); the order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no period, \"until\" date, condition or provisional approval that limits the approval, and no stay or postponement to a fixed date. The Construction Industry Code was approved January 31, 1934 (EO 6578). A search of the held 1933-1935 order texts for \"Construction Industry\" finds, besides EO 6578 and this order, the approvals of sibling chapters (EO 6606-D, 6640, 6684-E, 6711-B, 6750-B, 6988, 7025), EO 6731 (June 6, 1934, appointing a chairman of the code's Planning and Adjustment Board) and many orders approving labor agreements of code divisions (EO 6813 through EO 7036). I read the operative sentence of EO 6731 and of the chapter approvals EO 6606-D, 6640, 6684-E and 6711-B (each approves a further chapter and modifies the parent approval to cover the code as supplemented); none cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the Electrical Contracting Chapter or the parent code, and the one cancellation order found in that search (EO 6925, December 19, 1934) cancels the approval of a different code (Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade). I did not read the labor-agreement orders; by title they approve agreements among members of code divisions, which are separate section 7(b) instruments that this analysis does not decide, and none is titled as a cancellation of the code. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.","independent_command_check":"No appointment, delegation, direction to a government agency, report direction or other command independent of the code approval appears. The \"Approval recommended\" and signature lines command nothing.","savings_check":"Read S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso and NIRA section 5 in the packet excerpts. No held source continues this approval, a prosecution under it or any command of this order after June 14, 1935; accrued acts, liabilities and the section 5 exemption for completed action are recorded as transferred or accrued and not as continued operation.","scope_check":"One operative command with two parts that depend on each other: approval of the Electrical Contracting Chapter and modification of the previous approval of the Construction Industry Code to include that code as supplemented. Both act only through the section 3 approval of the code as supplemented, so one clause covers them."}

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, held the code provisions in question invalid on both of its grounds; recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date for this order. It adjudicated the Live Poultry Code provisions and cancelled or withdrew no other approving order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: date the Act was approved; states the repealed legal effects of a code approval, not an end date
source_notes.reason: Sections 3(a)-(f) state the legal effects of an approved code that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed: the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition (3(b)), district courts could restrain violations (3(c)), and violations were misdemeanors (3(f)).
